item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong direct evidence for disaster relief, child/women support, anti-discrimination, and restitution for past abuses. Direct evidence on health-system reform and broader welfare-state redesign in 2024 was thinner than the evidence on disaster response, redistribution, and rights repair. The main negative evidence is structural rather than personal: some institutions, especially criminal justice, still failed basic welfare-protective standards.","evidence":[{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-30","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"Kishida put wage growth, child support, disaster recovery, women’s participation, public education, dementia policy, and regional revitalization at the center of his 2024 agenda, which is strong evidence that human welfare was a core governing purpose.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.1","5B.6"]},{"title":"Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the Package of Measures to Support the Daily Lives and the Livelihoods of the Disaster Victims and Other Matters","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-25","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html","summary":"The package included cash aid, housing support, and direct relief for disaster victims, with explicit attention to low-income households, healthcare, childcare, schools, transit, SMEs, agriculture, and tourism.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.1","5B.8","5B.9"]},{"title":"Instructions by the Prime Minister Regarding the Earthquake Centered in Ishikawa Prefecture","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-01","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/decisions/2024/0101shiji.html","summary":"Kishida ordered timely warnings, evacuation, damage prevention, and emergency response with human life first. That is direct evidence that welfare and life protection were treated as primary state duties.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.6","5B.9"]},{"title":"Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-11","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/11kaiken.html","summary":"He explicitly recommended secondary evacuation for vulnerable groups, citing winter conditions, congestion, and infection risk. This is strong welfare-centered crisis management.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.9","4B.7"]},{"title":"Press Conference by the Prime Minister on His Visit to Ishikawa Prefecture","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-02-24","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/24kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida announced support for traditional industries, temporary workshops at national expense, and new household aid for affected families, including young households and families with children.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-06-21","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida backed expanded subsidies aimed at school lunches, agriculture, SMEs, medical and care services, childcare, public transport, logistics, and regional tourism, plus energy subsidies for low-income households.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.1","5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"Video Message by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio on International Women’s Day","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-03-08","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/08message2.html","summary":"He committed to narrowing wage gaps, increasing women in executive roles, supporting work-family balance, and strengthening protections for women facing violence or compounded hardship.","question_ids":["6B.1","4B.7","5B.8"]},{"title":"Statement on Forced Sterilization Redress","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-07-03","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/03kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida called the former Eugenics Protection Law unconstitutional, expressed sincere remorse and profound apology, and promised compensation and new guarantees. That is direct, welfare-oriented state accountability.","question_ids":["6B.1","4B.7","5B.5"]},{"title":"Statement on Human Rights / Inclusive Society","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-02-05","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html","summary":"Kishida explicitly rejected discrimination and violence against foreigners, Ainu people, sexual minorities, and people with disabilities, and tied policy to human dignity and the rule of law.","question_ids":["6B.1","4B.7","4B.10"]},{"title":"Statement on democracy, rights, women, and child rights","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-03-20","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/20message.html","summary":"Kishida framed human rights, women’s empowerment, and child rights as pillars of a peaceful, stable society, which is directly consistent with treating human welfare as a core purpose.","question_ids":["6B.1","4B.7","4B.10"]},{"title":"“Illegal foreigners zero” page","publisher":"Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site","date":"2024","url":"https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/","summary":"The tougher migrant-control line, including stricter screening, deportation enforcement, and tighter refugee procedures, is a mixed negative signal because it narrows access and treats some groups more punitively rather than expanding shared welfare.","question_ids":["6B.1","4B.7","5B.4"]},{"title":"Japan’s abusive hostage justice system persists","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-10-01","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/01/japans-abusive-hostage-justice-system-persists","summary":"HRW’s critique of coercive detention and weak correction mechanisms is negative structural evidence: it suggests Kishida did not transform all state institutions into welfare-protecting ones, even if this was not a direct rejection of welfare as a purpose.","question_ids":["6B.1","4B.10","4B.7"]}]}
